title: route-aware safety
claim: Track1-only mode is legacy-independent at strategy + safety scheduler wiring level.
claim_limits: NOT safe to delete legacy before the 5P shadow period passes
broker-flat / orphan-STP cleanliness NOT measured against IBKR - those are account-level statements and nothing here consulted the broker
closes: audit blocker L3; the one legacy dependency the 5M-D removability probe measured

legacy_safety_inventory.fate_in_track1_only: KEPT - drain. Any open legacy position keeps its stop repair and five-day exit. Removing it is part of deleting legacy, gated on 5P

track1_safety.shape: max-hold 09:31 (the backtest's 09:30-bar exit convention, unchanged) + 9 weekday sweeps at :20 + Sunday 18:30
track1_safety.sweep_derivation: from REQUIRED_ENTRY_WINDOWS - no sweep inside any Track 1 entry window; excludes hours 2 (NKD band), 12 (Stress), 14 (swing)
track1_safety.path_identity: TRACK1_POSITIONS_PATH/STOP_PATH asserted equal to the entry point's own POSITIONS_PATH/STOP_FILE constants
track1_safety.client_id_reasoning: legacy safety dials 1; Track 1 data slots dial 89; a sweep firing while the 10:00 Calm slot still holds 89 must not collide - so 90
track1_safety.registered: track1-only mode ONLY. Transitional mode unchanged: legacy safety already watches the only book that can hold positions there
track1_safety.shadow_cost: run_maxhold_exit returns before connecting when the positions file is absent, so a pure shadow period costs one short-lived process per job
track1_safety.catch_up: _catch_up_maxhold_track1, reading ONLY the Track 1 marker; fires only when the job exists (track1-only)

proven: the Track 1 run records into its own file and leaves legacy's untouched
the legacy marker does NOT suppress the Track 1 catch-up
the Track 1 marker DOES suppress its own catch-up
outside track1-only the catch-up is a no-op
marker_separation.why: a shared already-ran-today file is how one route's run silently suppresses the other's sweep and a five-day position stays open - the audit's named failure

ops.status: track1_safety_routes reports which route's safety net is scheduled, read from the RUNNING process's command line; track1-only-shadow mode is distinguished from the transitional mode

harness_defect_found.what: the first mutation run reported 4/8 detected - S1-S4 (on-disk edits of run_scheduler.py) all UNDETECTED
harness_defect_found.why: the harness ran pytest.main in-process; the mutated module was already cached in sys.modules, so the tests exercised pre-mutation code while the disk said otherwise. The mutation was unfaithful, not the tests
harness_defect_found.fix: on-disk mutations now run pytest in a FRESH subprocess, as an operator's pytest would; in-process monkeypatch mutations keep pytest.main (a subprocess would never see them). 8/8 after the split

mutations.mutation: S1 Track 1 stop repair points at live_positions.json again
S2 Track 1 max-hold writes the shared maxhold_state.json again
S3 the legacy marker suppresses the Track 1 catch-up
S4 the route env vanishes from the Track 1 safety children
S5 the Track 1 safety jobs are absent from track1-only
S6 a legacy strategy job survives track1-only
S7 a hardcoded '== 11' count returns to the wiring
S8 a sweep lands inside a Track 1 entry window

tests.stale_updates: 5 assertions in the 5M-D suite scoped to strategy slots (the safety argv is a different contract: no --sleeve, --port legitimate) and bucket/mirror counts extended by the safety jobs

no_side_effects: no live state written - maxhold_state.track1.json does NOT exist; every marker test ran against tmp_path
